title: Questionnaire flow overview
purpose: Define the eight steps, their order and the conditions under which each step and question appears. Cover saving and resuming, going back without losing answers, discarding answers that no longer apply, the permit reminder, the summary and confirmation, and read-only after submission.

stories.title: Show the source tax step only to employees who are subject to source tax
stories.i_want: the source tax details (denomination, whether the spouse is gainfully employed, whether there are children) and the children step to be asked only of employees who are subject to source tax, and for Liechtenstein residents only when they stay abroad more than 45 non-return days
stories.so_that: I no longer have to guess up front who must answer the source tax questions, and Lonio holds no source tax data about people who do not need it
stories.priority_reason: HR names this as a current pain ('I never know up front who has to answer those questions'), and asking everyone breaks data minimisation (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Source tax details only for employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered the steps 'Home address', 'Nationality and C permit' and 'Civil status and spouse'
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether to show step 6 'Source tax details'
acceptance_criteria.then: the step is shown only if the employee is subject to source tax (anyone living abroad; or, living in Switzerland, a non-Swiss employee without a C permit who is not married or in a registered partnership with a Swiss national or C-permit holder living in Switzerland). Otherwise denomination, spouse gainfully employed and has children are not asked, and step 7 'Children' is not shown either.

examples.name: Stefan, Swiss living abroad, country assumed Germany (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a)
Non-Swiss, no C permit, single, living in Switzerland
Non-Swiss in a registered partnership with a non-Swiss partner without C permit

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse gainfully employed only for married employees and registered partners
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is shown step 6 'Source tax details'
acceptance_criteria.then: the question whether the spouse or registered partner is gainfully employed is asked only if the civil status is Married or Registered partnership; Separated counts as single for source tax, so separated, single, divorced and widowed employees are not asked it (assumption D-003, to be verified by a domain expert).

acceptance_criteria.title: Liechtenstein residents: cross-border questions first, tariff questions only above 45 non-return days
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee lives in Liechtenstein (and is therefore subject to source tax)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: step 5 'Cross-border commuting' (daily return, then more than 45 non-return days) comes before step 6 'Source tax details'. If the employee returns daily or expects at most 45 non-return days, there is in principle no source tax liability and steps 6 and 7 are skipped. If the employee expects more than 45 non-return days, steps 6 and 7 are asked as for any employee subject to source tax. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): this order and skipping follow D-040.

examples.name: Liechtenstein, no daily return, at most 45 days
Liechtenstein, no daily return, more than 45 days

stories.title: Ask the steps in an order that avoids unneeded questions
stories.i_want: to go through eight fixed steps in a fixed order, where each step and each question appears only when a receiving party needs my answer
stories.so_that: I answer only what is needed, and earlier answers (where I live, my nationality, my civil status) decide which later questions I see
stories.priority_reason: The flow is the backbone of the questionnaire: asking too little blocks a registration, asking too much collects personal data no party needs (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Exactly eight steps in a fixed order
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee opens the questionnaire, which is in English
acceptance_criteria.then: the steps come in this order: 1 About you; 2 Home address; 3 Nationality and C permit; 4 Civil status and spouse; 5 Cross-border commuting; 6 Source tax details; 7 Children; 8 Permit reminder, summary and submission. There is no separate step for the first working day. A step whose questions all do not apply to this employee is skipped. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): this list of steps and its order follow D-047.

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 1 'About you' for everyone
acceptance_criteria.given: any employee
acceptance_criteria.then: first name, last name, date of birth and first working day are required of everyone.

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 2 'Home address' as on the first working day; canton only in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: any employee
acceptance_criteria.then: the home address as it applies on the first working day is required: street, house number (or the explicit option 'no house number'), postcode, town and country. The canton is asked only if the country is Switzerland. Assumptions (to be verified by a domain expert): the address applies on the first working day (D-041), every address field is required apart from the 'no house number' option (D-042, D-049), and employees abroad are not asked for a canton (D-002).

examples.name: Stefan, Swiss living abroad, country assumed Germany (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a)

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 3 'Nationality and C permit' only for employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has given the country of the home address
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether to show step 3
acceptance_criteria.then: nationality is asked only if the employee lives in Switzerland; employees living abroad are subject to source tax whatever their nationality and are not asked it. Whether the employee holds a C permit (yes/no) is asked only if the nationality is not Switzerland; no other permit type is asked. Anyone holding Swiss citizenship, also together with another nationality, answers Switzerland.

examples.name: Stefan, Swiss living abroad, country assumed Germany (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a)

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 4 'Civil status and spouse': civil status for everyone, spouse questions only when needed
acceptance_criteria.given: any employee, wherever they live
acceptance_criteria.then: civil status is required of everyone. The spouse's or registered partner's date of birth is asked only if the civil status is Married, Registered partnership or Separated, not if Divorced or Widowed (assumption D-004, to be verified by a domain expert). The spouse's nationality, whether the spouse holds a C permit (only if the spouse is not Swiss) and whether the spouse lives in Switzerland (only if the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit) are asked only of a non-Swiss employee living in Switzerland without a C permit who is married or in a registered partnership, because only then can the spouse exemption from source tax apply.

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 5 'Cross-border commuting' only for Liechtenstein and Germany residents
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has given the country of the home address
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether to show step 5
acceptance_criteria.then: the step is shown only to employees living in Liechtenstein or Germany, who are all subject to source tax. Liechtenstein residents are asked about daily return and, without daily return, about more than 45 non-return days; Germany residents are asked about daily return and the follow-up questions (including the certificate of residence). The employee states what they expect for the year; no documents are uploaded. Employees living in Switzerland or in any other country do not see this step.

acceptance_criteria.title: Steps 6 and 7 only when source tax details apply; one block per child
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is subject to source tax and, if living in Liechtenstein, expects more than 45 non-return days
acceptance_criteria.then: step 6 asks denomination, spouse gainfully employed (married and registered partners only) and whether the employee has biological or adopted children. Step 7 'Children' is shown only if the answer is yes, with one block of child questions per child; there is no maximum number of children and each child's age is judged on the first working day (assumption D-044, to be verified by a domain expert).

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 8 closes the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered every step that applies
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee sees the permit reminder if it applies to them, then a summary page, and submits with one confirmation.

stories.title: Ask each piece of information once and reuse it for every receiving party
stories.i_want: each piece of information to be asked once in the questionnaire and recorded for every receiving party that needs it (pension fund, source tax and HR)
stories.so_that: the employee is not asked the same thing twice and I no longer collect the data separately for each party and re-enter it
stories.priority_reason: Core goal of the feature (G-01): collect once, reuse for every party; today data is collected per party and re-entered manually.

acceptance_criteria.title: No question appears twice
acceptance_criteria.given: a piece of information is needed by more than one party (for example civil status by the pension fund and for source tax, or the country of residence by HR, the pension fund and source tax)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the question is asked once, in its step, and the single answer is recorded for HR and used for every party that needs it; for example civil status is asked once in step 4 and serves both the pension fund registration and the source tax tariff.

examples.name: Civil status asked once for everyone

acceptance_criteria.title: Derived values are not asked
acceptance_criteria.given: a value one party needs can be derived from answers already given
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not asked for it: the insurance start date is derived from the first working day, the canton for employees living abroad is set to the canton of the place of work (Zurich), the civil status for the pension fund and for source tax is derived from the one civil status answer, and the source tax tariff code is computed from the answers. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): the canton for employees abroad follows D-002 and the civil status mapping follows D-003.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers are recorded for HR
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: they are recorded for HR; how they are passed to the pension fund and the source tax office, and any HR screen, are specified separately.

stories.title: Remind non-Swiss employees and employees living abroad to bring their permit
stories.i_want: every non-Swiss employee living in Switzerland and every employee living abroad to be reminded at the end of the questionnaire to bring their permit on the first working day
stories.so_that: fewer new employees forget their permit on their first day
stories.priority_reason: Explicit HR wish ('Half of them forget'); it saves follow-up but does not block a registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Who sees the reminder
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reaches step 8 'Permit reminder, summary and submission'
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether to show the permit reminder
acceptance_criteria.then: the reminder is shown to an employee living in Switzerland whose nationality is not Switzerland, and to every employee living abroad whatever their nationality (nationality is not asked of them). It is not shown to a Swiss employee living in Switzerland.

examples.name: Stefan, Swiss living abroad, country assumed Germany (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a)

acceptance_criteria.title: Wording provided by HR; Swiss citizens abroad can tell it does not apply
acceptance_criteria.given: the reminder is shown
acceptance_criteria.then: it uses the wording HR provides before go-live, and that wording lets a Swiss citizen living abroad, such as Stefan, see that it does not apply to them. The reminder only informs: it asks no question and collects no data.

stories.title: Discard answers that no longer apply on submission
stories.i_want: to go back and change an earlier answer without losing my other answers, while answers to questions that no longer apply are not kept once I submit
stories.so_that: I can correct myself freely, and Lonio keeps no personal data about me that no party needs
stories.priority_reason: Data minimisation is a hard constraint (G-01); losing input when going back would frustrate employees.

acceptance_criteria.title: Going back keeps answers until submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered questions in later steps and goes back to change an earlier answer so that some of those questions no longer apply
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee changes the answer back, or moves forward again, before submitting
acceptance_criteria.then: every answer given earlier is still there, including answers to questions that currently do not apply, so no input is lost by going back and forth before submission.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers that no longer apply are discarded on submission
acceptance_criteria.given: at submission some answers belong to questions that do not apply to the employee's latest answers
acceptance_criteria.then: those answers are discarded and are not recorded, shown on the record or used for any result; only answers to questions that apply are kept.

examples.name: Moved the home address from Germany to Switzerland before submitting; Germany cross-border and source tax answers are discarded
Changed civil status from Married to Divorced before submitting; spouse date of birth is discarded

stories.title: Make the questionnaire read-only after submission and derive results from the latest answers
stories.i_want: the questionnaire to be read-only for the employee once submitted, with later changes made by HR and every derived result always derived again from the latest answers
stories.so_that: the record stays consistent and the pension fund and source tax always get results that match the current facts
stories.priority_reason: Prevents inconsistent records after submission; the HR editing itself is specified later (D-034).

acceptance_criteria.title: Read-only for the employee after submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee can see the answers but cannot change them; any later change (a move, a marriage, a new child, a certificate of residence handed in later, a corrected nationality, a moved first working day) is made by HR, in the HR-side spec to be written later.

acceptance_criteria.title: Derived results always follow the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: an answer has changed after submission
acceptance_criteria.when: the derived results are looked at
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance start date, the civil status for the pension fund and for source tax, whether the employee is subject to source tax and the tariff code are derived again from the latest answers; for the first working day the latest date always counts and no history of earlier dates is kept.

examples.name: Tomás after HR records that his wife no longer lives in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: HR change that opens unanswered questions
acceptance_criteria.given: after submission HR changes an answer so that questions apply that the employee was never asked (for example the employee now becomes subject to source tax)
acceptance_criteria.when: the derived results that depend on those questions are looked at
acceptance_criteria.then: they show 'incomplete - HR must complete' instead of a value (for example the tariff code) until HR enters the missing answers. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): this follows D-048.

acceptance_criteria.title: HR change that makes answers no longer apply
acceptance_criteria.given: after submission HR changes an answer so that some recorded answers no longer apply
acceptance_criteria.then: the answers that no longer apply are discarded, as on the employee's submission. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): this follows D-048.

stories.title: Save answers as I go and resume until I submit
stories.i_want: my answers to be saved as I go, so that I can stop and come back to the questionnaire until I submit it
stories.so_that: I can look up information (for example my spouse's date of birth or my expected non-return days) without losing what I have already entered
stories.priority_reason: Convenience for the employee; it does not change which data is collected.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers are saved as the employee goes
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered some questions and leaves the questionnaire before submitting
acceptance_criteria.then: all answers given so far are still there and the employee can continue and submit. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): this follows D-050.

acceptance_criteria.title: Resuming ends with submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee can no longer change answers; the questionnaire is read-only and later changes are made by HR.

stories.title: Review a summary and submit with one confirmation
stories.i_want: to see a summary of my answers and submit them with one confirmation
stories.so_that: I can check what I give before it is recorded for HR and used for the pension fund and source tax
stories.priority_reason: Submission completes the onboarding data; without it no registration or tariff code can be produced.

acceptance_criteria.title: Summary before submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered every step that applies and has seen the permit reminder if it applies
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the end of step 8
acceptance_criteria.then: a summary page shows the employee's answers. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): the summary shows only answers to questions that apply to the employee's latest answers, since the others will be discarded on submission (D-036, D-045).

acceptance_criteria.title: One confirmation submits
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is on the summary page
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire is submitted and the answers are recorded for HR; nothing is submitted before this confirmation.

acceptance_criteria.title: Required answers must be given before submission
acceptance_criteria.given: a question that applies and is required for this employee has no answer
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire is not submitted and the employee is shown which answers are missing. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): no source states this behaviour explicitly; it follows from the questions being required (D-045).
